utilities.name: Tinycast
utilities.summary: Native launcher, clipboard history, snippets and Raycast-compatible extensions.
utilities.notes: Extensions are opt-in and compatibility varies by extension. Configure its shortcut yourself to avoid overlap with Hangar.

utilities.name: Shottr
utilities.summary: Screenshot annotation, scrolling capture, OCR and pixel measurements.
utilities.pricing: Free use with reminders; paid license required for commercial use
utilities.notes: The current Homebrew cask requires macOS 12+. Screen Recording permission and any paid license are configured in Shottr. Its preferences control telemetry.

utilities.name: Thaw
utilities.summary: Hide, reveal and arrange menu bar items, with a separate Thaw Bar.
utilities.notes: Signed and notarized. Accessibility is needed for arranging items; Screen Recording is optional. Keep existing layouts and preferences.

utilities.name: LocalSend
utilities.summary: Transfer files and text between nearby Macs, phones and other computers over the local network.
utilities.notes: Choose when you share with Android, Windows or Linux devices. Both devices need LocalSend and local network access. Hangar does not change firewall rules, allow incoming transfers or enable login launch.

utilities.name: IINA
utilities.summary: Media playback for local video and audio files, with broad format support through mpv.
utilities.notes: Choose when QuickTime does not cover your formats or playback controls. Apple silicon requires macOS 12; Intel supports 11. The Homebrew cask also links the iina command. Hangar does not change default file associations or install plugins.

utilities.name: Stats
utilities.summary: Optional menu bar monitoring for CPU, memory, disks and network; polls while running.
utilities.notes: Choose only if you want continuous monitoring. Periodic reads cost CPU and energy; disable unneeded modules, especially Sensors and Bluetooth. Fan control is unmaintained upstream. Hangar does not configure a privileged helper, fan control, remote monitoring or login items.

utilities.name: Mole
utilities.summary: Optional terminal toolkit for Mac maintenance; Hangar opens its live status dashboard only.
utilities.pricing: Free and open-source CLI; native Mole app is a separate product
utilities.notes: Installs the mo command via a Homebrew formula. Hangar opens only mo status in Terminal. Mole also has destructive cleanup and optimization commands; these are not exposed here. Its disk analyzer can move selected files to Trash after confirmation. Existing installations are preserved without upgrade.
